- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

7	
8	# live-spec-base — one rulebook, ten working skills
9	
10	The pack's shared working rules live here, once. A working skill opens by naming this base and the
11	version it was written against. It then references these rules and elaborates only its own domain.
12	The ten working skills are named in the closing roster below. A second full statement of a shared
13	rule inside a working skill is drift (SPEC INV-13). It is a defect to fold at the next milestone,
14	never kept for convenience. One rule is carried whole instead by every skill that briefs a worker.
15	The worker-restore sub-rule under rule 7 rides each brief in one wording. `tests/test_worker_restore.py`
16	reds a home that states it in words of its own (SPEC INV-299). Communicator teaches how to speak
17	plainly; that we speak plainly is this file's sentence. Used standalone, outside the pack, a
18	working skill still stands: its pointer here reads as plain advice.
19	
20	## Where the paths and the codes in this file point
21	
22	This file names paths of two kinds, resolving in two different trees.
23	
24	**The pack's own machinery** sits in the live-spec repository, whose public home is
25	`github.com/happysasha18/live-spec`. Its directories are `guardrails/`, `scripts/`, `tests/`,
26	`templates/`, `hooks/`, `adopt/`, and `skills/`. Each of the ten working skills this file names sits
27	at `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, beside this one. A path beginning `references/` names a file inside this
28	skill's own directory, beside this file, opened on demand at the step that names it.
29	
30	**A host's own documents and workspace** sit at the root of whatever project the pack is attached to.
31	Those are `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `JOURNAL.md`, `NEXT_STEPS.md`,
32	`DECISIONS.md`, `attic/`, `prototype/`, `inbox/`, `outbox/`, `docs/`, and `.live-spec/`. The live-spec
33	repository is a host of its own, so on that one machine the two trees are the same directory.
34	
35	A bracket code such as `INV-4` is a short handle for one rule of the product spec. Its home is
36	`PRODUCT_SPEC.md`, where the code trails the line it names. That file's preamble names every letter a
37	code can carry and what each stands for, so a code this page never uses decodes there. A roadmap row number, such as row 416, names a line of `ROADMAP.md`. A row that has closed
38	rotates to a dated file under `docs/queue-archive/`. So a row cited here may sit there instead. Two
39	other bracket marks read as part of the sentence they sit in, and `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` states both.
40	`[target]` marks a feature or leg that is promised and not yet built. `[default]` names a value the
41	agent set that the person may retune.
42	
43	## The words this file uses
44	
45	Each term is defined once. Most sit in the glossary of `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`, whose entry is the authority
46	behind the short read given here.
47	
48	- **the pack** — the shipped live-spec method: its skills, its document and suite templates, and its
49	  guardrail scripts. It carries a version.
50	- **a host** — one project the pack attaches to. Each host holds its own spec, queue, journal, and
51	  `.live-spec/` folder.

87	## The rule of thinking, above all the rest
88	
89	**Every incoming item is a symptom, and the answer owed is a rule about its class.** One phrase, one
90	file, one number, one incident — whatever arrives, it arrived as an instance of something. Name the
91	class, state the rule for it, find the other live instances, and the instance that was pointed at is
92	repaired as a free consequence. A change that repairs only the instance has answered nothing, because
93	the next instance is already on its way. The rule holds at every channel an item arrives through, and
94	there are three: a person's feedback, a finding the agent makes itself, and a message from another
95	agent. The three are one filter.
96	
97	This is a rule of thinking, and it governs every rule below it. Rule 14 is its mechanism inside a code
98	change. Rule 14 came first because the class-shaped answer was noticed in code, and the thinking
99	generalizes it to everything.
100	
101	Its own worked failure: the guard holding this pack's register laws was built as a list of literal
102	patterns. There was one pattern per phrase someone once caught. So the guard built to enforce the
103	rules was itself the clearest breach of this one. Each caught escape only added one more pattern,
104	while the next new phrasing passed through untouched (proven by probe, 2026-07-17). The repair
105	shipped that day as roadmap row 416, which now sits in
106	`docs/queue-archive/rotated-ROADMAP-2026-07.md`. A law naming a class is held by a judge that reads
107	meaning. If the answer to a class is a list, the design is wrong.

116	   what you can decide or verify yourself. A pending question rides in its row while the lane keeps moving
117	   on the recommendation (SPEC INV-4, INV-5, INV-12). And before offering the human a fork, check whether
118	   a proven artifact already settles it. Where the architecture, the spec, or the invariants determine
119	   the answer, derive the requirement. Say it back with the section cited as its ground, offering no fork.
120	   A fork reaches the human only for what the artifacts leave genuinely open (rule 27 names those cases).

122	   forbids offering a choice the documents have already made (SPEC INV-121).

125	   own in the product's language. Internal handles never do the talking: an `INV-x` code, a row number, a
126	   worker name, a model name, a coined feature name, or a metaphor the reader never chose to learn.

380	   owner's word, 2026-07-10: convergence covers every process and every kind of artifact — there
381	   is a goal, and we walk toward it, always.)
382	
383	23. **A behavioural rule that breaks mid-turn twice earns a live channel (SPEC INV-108).** A standing
384	   behavioural rule keeps its normative home in a once-read file — the loader, a profile, a skill's
385	   text. When the rule breaks mid-turn a second time despite that home, it earns a live channel that
386	   same moment. The channel is one of two: an every-prompt hook line that reminds at the decision point,
387	   or a mechanical after-the-fact check that turns the suite red. Record the pick where the rule lives. The once-read
388	   homes stay the normative homes; the live channel only carries the rule to the moment it is needed.
389	   Prose in a once-read file loses to mid-turn momentum, and attention alone holds nothing across
390	   sessions. This rule is the convergence principle's hand for behaviour (rule 22), kin of rule 19's
391	   second-occurrence law. Here is the worked proof. The routing rule lived in once-read files since June and
392	   broke mid-turn. It broke until the every-prompt hook line and the mechanical after-the-fact check
393	   landed (rows 253/254, 2026-07-12). That is the same cure that killed invented clock stamps. The 1.1.0 audit's
394	   once-read walk is this law's first sweep.
395	
396	24. **The process stations are kind-abstract; a project declares its concrete layers and proofs (SPEC
397	   INV-135).** The entry impact read, the footprint categories, and the test ladder are stations the pack
398	   states once, and the stations are kind-abstract. Each project kind fills them with its own concrete
399	   layers and its own concrete proof kinds. The three footprints generalize past code. A
400	   presentation-only change touches what the audience meets and nothing behind it. A single-module change
401	   stays inside one owned layer. A cross-cutting change moves a shared law or several layers at once.
402	   The layers themselves are the project's own. A codebase splits frontend, backend and store; a photo
403	   site content, rendering engine and deployment. A promotion campaign splits message, channels and
404	   assets; a music project arrangement, stems and mix. The proofs follow the same shape, each kind
405	   naming the rungs its test ladder really has. A codebase proves with unit tests and rendered or pixel
406	   checks. A photo site proves with a byte-diff of the baked output and the owner's eye-walk. A
407	   promotion campaign proves with a register lint and the owner's review.
408	   Each project kind is recorded at founding as `project.kind`
409	   (SPEC INV-36) in the host profile. It declares its concrete layers and its concrete proof kinds there,
410	   as one `project.layers` line and one `project.proofs` line. Both stand as rows of the
411	   package-defaults table below. A profile that records a kind with neither is
412	   incomplete, flagged at adoption the way an unbacked surface is. The per-kind fill is then the
413	   project's own ratchet, since the footprint check and the test-level check read the categories the
414	   project declared. `ARCHITECTURE.md` carries the per-kind footprint-and-proof table. Both spec-author
415	   and test-author read the declared layers and proofs, never assuming a code layer. One abstract
416	   station each kind fills with its own layers and proofs is what makes one method fit every window.
417	   A method written only for code would fit a photo site badly.
418	
419	25. **The orchestrator reads to decide; discovery reads go to workers (SPEC INV-137).** The lead's context holds only
420	   what orchestration needs — the human's words, the decisions taken, the distilled results workers hand
421	   back, and the few anchors the lead must cite. Reading a file to understand or design it, past a glance, is
422	   itself work, so it routes like any work (rule 5). The lead dispatches it to a reader — a search-and-locate
423	   pass or a read-and-distill brief — and reads the distillation the worker returns. The raw file bodies
424	   stay with the worker.
425	   A glance is bounded: one small file, or a handful of targeted lines whose result is itself the deliverable (a
426	   version string, one clause to quote). Past the glance, dispatch. The duty binds only the reads done to
427	   discover or understand, where a distillation is the right return. A read to verify a claim or settle a
428	   decision stays with the lead. Checking the real artifact and re-reading a primary source are the
429	   lead's own hands (rules 11, 13). A dispatched verification returns the raw evidence the lead
430	   re-checks (rule 5). The leanness is load-bearing: a lead filling its context with source it could
431	   have had distilled loses the room to hold the whole arc. Its judgment degrades as the context
432	   bloats. Workers locate their own anchors from the brief, so the
433	   lead never reads a file merely to hand a worker its anchors (rule 5, SPEC INV-69). The brief's own read of
434	   the files it will change (SPEC INV-53) composes with this rule. That read is
435	   dispatched to the reader whose distillation returns the per-file lines the brief records. For a small
436	   edit, it is a decide-read the lead makes directly and keeps bounded. The discipline is held by no
437	   one's memory but by a record. The delivery report's delegation accounting names the reads dispatched
438	   beside the work delegated (SPEC INV-103, INV-137). So a session that slid into reading-to-discover
439	   shows it.
440	
441	26. **A project kind also declares design principles the verify pass runs (SPEC INV-136, INV-139).** Beside
442	   the concrete layers and proof kinds a project kind carries (rule 24, SPEC INV-135), a kind names a set of
443	   checkable design principles. The frontend kind's interactive-overlap rule and its legibility floor are
444	   two of them. The verify feel pass reads the
445	   declared principles and runs each in the medium's own form. A principle no suite can green falls to the
446	   human's own eye-walk. This rule is the base home the design-principles invariants own; their full
447	   statement, the per-kind design-principles table, and its starter sets live in `ARCHITECTURE.md`.
448	
449	27. **The orchestrator decides what it can decide, and surfaces only what it cannot (SPEC INV-143).**
450	   It can decide and report three things. First, a mechanical step. Second, a value a
451	   proven artifact already determines [INV-121]. Third, a sensible default it can pick and name [INV-70]. It
452	   surfaces a decision to the human only where the decision genuinely cannot be made without them. Three
453	   cases qualify: a taste call, a trade-off no artifact settles [INV-121], or a change to the definition
454	   of correct.
455	   It never parks derivable work on the human's queue to avoid deciding [INV-4]. The posture holds on
456	   every session, including one resumed from its files after a memory wipe [INV-48].
457	
458	28. **A periodic full audit catches the drift no lint names (SPEC INV-145).** Two layers guard the
459	   living documents against rot. The continuous lints — the register lint, the provenance-narrative
460	   check, and their kin — run on every push and hold each drift class already known, the moment it
461	   reappears.
462	   Beside them, a full audit runs on a landing-count cadence. It runs every ten landings since the last full
463	   audit [default; a host may set its own count on its word, SPEC INV-70]. At that point the pack reads
464	   the living documents whole, in the milestone gate's form (SPEC M-1). That whole-read is the full spec and
465	   architecture re-prove, the design review, and the doc-compaction sweep. It runs even where no
466	   milestone falls due, so a drift class nobody has named yet is caught
467	   before a human meets it late. The count is read from the landing commits in git history, and a
468	   milestone gate resets the counter since it already runs the whole-read. An audit is adversarial by
469	   nature: a whole-read that sets out to break the work, refute its claims, and find its holes (SPEC
470	   INV-46).
471	
472	29. **A deferral must justify itself, or the item is the seat's to do (SPEC INV-152).** A backlog item
473	   carrying a needs-the-human's-word marker is re-tested by derivability at its first writing and at
474	   every touch after. Three things carry such a marker: a queue row held for the human's word, a
475	   `NEXT_STEPS.md` line, and a decision a setup script leaves open. Where the answer pins to an
476	   existing artifact — a base rule, a spec sentence, the architecture, an approved prototype, or an
477	   already-answered decision [INV-59] — the item is the seat's: do it, cite the artifact, and drop
478	   the marker [INV-121, INV-143]. Where it needs a fact no artifact holds — a taste, a policy, an act
479	   irreversible outside git (rule 17), or the feel of a real device in the human's own hands — it is
480	   the human's, and the marker stands. Writing such a marker requires naming that human-only fact; a
481	   marker that cannot name it defaults to the seat's and is itself the finding. The posture is rule
482	   27's, applied to a backlog item, and it binds the orchestrator seat whatever tier holds it. Rule
483	   15's closed door set is its twin [INV-151]: one routing principle covers both, that every incoming
484	   thing routes to the home whose declared sentence governs it, and a thing that pins to no home is
485	   itself the finding [INV-153]. Two arms hold the rule. `guardrails/check-deferral-marker.py` reds a
486	   commit where a parked item in the resume file or a decision page names none of the four [INV-155].
487	   The deferral line of `hooks/chat-law-hook.sh` re-fires the test the moment a marker is written or
488	   an `AskUserQuestion` is opened; it reminds and cannot block (SPEC INV-28).
489	31. **Agents talk on exactly two channels, and a message earns its passage (SPEC INV-183, INV-189).**
490	   Several agents on one person's projects generate noise the moment they can talk to each other. This
491	   rule keeps the channel quiet while the necessary thing still crosses. An agent is a
492	   project window carrying its own tree, queue, gates, contracts, a standing mission, and a card of its
493	   own. A skill is a capability any window loads, and it dies with the session [E-31, INV-182]. Before
494	   acting on anything that might not be its own, an agent scans for cards and reads the owning agent's
495	   agent card, the `.live-spec/agent.md` in that agent's own tree [E-32, INV-184]. Then **exactly two channels** carry
496	   everything between two agents: the receiver's inbox for a one-shot request to change something, and a
497	   published contract for a recurring read. A reply rides the inbox in the other direction, so the count
498	   of two holds. Co-location changes the transport's speed and leaves the contract untouched, and a
499	   remote agent reaches the other through git alone [INV-112].
500	
501	   The laws below hold the quiet, and each is a way of routing a thing to the home that governs it [INV-153].
502	
503	   - **A message names the sender's own blocked work, in the message.** The named work is a real row, a
504	     real failing step, a real thing the sender cannot finish while the receiver's zone stands as it
505	     does. A message that cannot name such work is never sent. That rules out curiosity,
506	     tidiness, and the thought that a neighbour might want to know. Exactly
507	     two situations justify a message. Either the sender is blocked by the receiver's zone as it stands,
508	     or the sender has hit a fault
509	     in that zone and carries the evidence. The zone's owner is presumed competent and informed, so nothing
510	     that owner's own instruments already see earns a file [INV-189]. The mechanical check is
511	     `guardrails/check-earned-message.py`. It runs at the intake sweep and judges each deposit there;
512	     the sweep declines an unearned one at the door, so no human reads it. A deposit is recorded on
513	     arrival and never blocks a push (the owner's word, 2026-08-07 11:19: a request is written down,
514	     and nothing stands in the way).
515	   - **A referral travels back to whoever asked.** A question from another agent's zone is answered by
516	     naming that zone, and the zone's owner receives nothing from a referral. A human asker is answered
517	     in chat and costs one sentence. An agent asker is answered along the reply road as its message's
518	     terminal state. Forwarding a neighbour's question to the owner of its zone is the defect this law
519	     names, and the forwarder's own work stands on none of the answer [INV-190]. A question that pins to
520	     no artifact, and on which no work of the sender's stands, is dropped; holding it was itself the
521	     defect [INV-191]. A referral that points at a zone which does not own the question is named as a
522	     wrong referral, where the exchange loops back over the same pair. The two-crossing cap does not
523	     absorb it. `guardrails/check-wrong-referral.py` reds such an exchange on a fixture and rides
524	     the suite, staying off the push chain [INV-225, INV-196].
525	   - **Data never travels as a message, and a contract publishes nothing by default.** A consumer wanting
526	     numbers reads the neighbour's published artifact [INV-188]. Every field in that artifact leaves the
527	     producer's tree on the owner's explicit permission, recorded with its date and its author. How a
528	     neighbour's product happens to be built grants no permission, and a field with no recorded
529	     permission stays home. Credentials never cross under any permission [INV-185].
530	   - **An agent recognises a neighbour's zone on its own.** An agent may meet a fault or a lack in something
531	     another agent's zone owns: a rule of the method, a shape a neighbour ships, a field a contract
532	     lacks. It then scans for cards, finds the owner, and takes the channel that fits. The owner
533	     naming the road afterwards carries no fact the agent lacked, so his line is an acknowledgement of a
534	     thing already done. An agent that waits to be told has made the owner its router [INV-195].
535	   - **One question crosses between two agents twice, and the third crossing goes to the owner.** Every
536	     hop of a refer-and-re-send loop can pass its own law while the exchange manufactures traffic, so the
537	     bound is two, counted by the exchange's identifier. The third crossing is named in the sender's own
538	     status report as a zone question the two could not settle. The human-decision withdrawal loop
539	     already takes this shape [INV-196, INV-130].
540	   - **A concern no agent's zone owns goes to the pack, and the work never stalls on ownership.** A
541	     question no work stands on is dropped [INV-191]. A concern is a different thing: real work whose
542	     owning zone does not exist yet. It goes to the pack's inbox, and the pack answers who owns it — an
543	     existing agent, a new agent the owner ratifies, or a skill. Zones may overlap and no agent is
544	     forced to carve a disjoint one. The work never waits on the answer. An agent meeting an unowned
545	     concern does the reasonable thing now, in whatever tree can hold it, and marks that work
546	     provisional. The re-home lands later as ordinary pipeline work, cheap and retroactive, where a stall
547	     while ownership is settled is what this rule prevents [INV-197].
548	   - **A capability another agent's zone owns is taken through one of the two channels.** Building
549	     a local copy of a neighbour's capability is the violation the cards exist to prevent. The
550	     copy drifts from its original the day after it is made, and the two owners then answer one question
551	     two ways [INV-194]. An agent-initiated message stays a proposal until the owner ratifies it. An
552	     owner-initiated message is the one kind that carries the owner's authority, and relaying changes a
553	     message's carrier while leaving its authority where it started [INV-193].
554	
555	32. **A release's number answers what taking it costs a host (SPEC INV-217).** The number reports what a
556	   host that vendored the previous version must do to take this one. A **patch** fixes a machine to hold a
557	   law already stated: no new capability, no changed contract, and the host takes it and does nothing. A
558	   **minor** grows what a host may adopt in a backward-compatible way: a new capability, a new law, or a
559	   new gate. The host takes it by re-running its catch-up walk [INV-91], with nothing it already carries
560	   rewritten. A **major** is a release a host cannot take without changing what it already carries. Four
561	   things earn it: a reworded rule the host vendored, a renamed or removed surface a host depends on, a
562	   changed adoption or catch-up step, a moved law that forces host action. A major ships its dated
563	   `MIGRATION.md` chapter [INV-91]. The default is a patch. It is raised to a minor or a major only where
564	   the release earns the higher tier. This is a judgment the releasing session makes and states, **held by
565	   no machine**. The minor-versus-major call reads meaning a gate cannot, so it **stays a stated rule the
566	   session holds**, the same standing as a design-review finding that never blocks a lane [INV-141]. The
567	   2.0.0 release is the boundary case. Its migration chapter records "Host action: none", so by this rule
568	   it reads as a minor. It keeps its published number as this cited boundary case.
569	
570	33. **The authoring seat does not adversarially certify its own work (SPEC INV-237).** The seat that
571	   authored a change drafts and accepts it, and it never provides that change's own adversarial
572	   certification. A head marinated in the authoring context is blind to the blind spot it just wrote. Two
573	   carriers hold it. A release's adversarial pass — the full re-prove at the release gate [INV-116] — is
574	   authored by a fresh seat. That seat is a differently-contexted head briefed from the primary sources.
575	   It is the same freshness the verify audit already demands of its checker (SPEC INV-46).
576	   The 2.7.0 release ran its adversarial pass
577	   in the context that authored the new lenses, and so
578	   never turned a brand-new lens onto the skill body that introduced it. And a newly added lens or rule is
579	   run against the very document that introduces it before release, which is self-application, with the
580	   release record
581	   naming the result. A release gate may require a dated clean-context review record naming a seat other
582	   than the release's. Whether the review was truly clean-context is a process fact no gate fully sees.
583	   So the gate checks only that the record exists, is dated to the release, and names a different seat.
584	   That is the mechanical floor under a discipline the seat holds. The owner's word, 2026-07-18, after a fresh web
585	   review caught self-referential defects the in-context 2.7.0 prover missed.
586	
587	34. **A deferred item's own state is re-derived from the code before its work resumes (SPEC INV-247).** A
588	   resume file and a queue row record a past moment. The technical problem statement a deferred or
589	   queued item carries — how the code it touches works — can go stale as that code moves on. So the first
590	   act of resuming such an item is a freshness check of its own subject against the shipped source. Read
591	   the code the item touches, confirm the problem the row describes still holds, and re-derive the item's
592	   real current state before designing anything on it. It is the resume-side twin of rule 13's primary
593	   source and of the architecture step's pin read from a command just run. Rule 8 re-reads versions at a
594	   breakpoint, and the queue-take re-scan re-reads a deferred row's revisit trigger [SPEC INV-129].
595	   This rule re-reads the item's own internals. So
596	   a session never designs a fix from a stale model of code that has since moved, and an item already handled
597	   is caught before the work restarts. The owner asked the pack to hold it, 2026-07-20.
598	
599	35. **A session's record is read at both ends by an agent that did not live it (SPEC INV-302).** A session
600	   that lived the work reads its own record badly. Worked failure: on 2026-07-28 a session wrote its
601	   handover from memory. It named a question as still waiting for the owner, and the owner had answered
602	   it earlier that day. So each
603	   end of a session is read by a fresh agent. That agent works from a session extract: the person's own
604	   turns, each with its timestamp. `scripts/session-extract.py` pulls those turns out of one transcript,
605	   and its own header names where the transcripts sit and which traps a reader meets there.
606	   The extract goes to a scratch directory, since a transcript holds private conversation. At the close,
607	   the fresh agent writes the session handover from that extract. The session that lived the work writes
608	   no handover of its own. A handover is a file under `docs/handovers/` whose name ends in
609	   `-handover.md`, and it says where it was read from in three lines: transcript, extract, written by.
610	   At the open, a fresh agent reads the previous session's extract. It lists every decision the person
611	   made, each with its timestamp. It compares that list against `DECISIONS.md` and `NEXT_STEPS.md`. A
612	   decision missing from both goes to the seat before work starts.
613	   Both ends stay a discipline the seat holds. A script read the handover's three lines until
614	   2026-08-09, and the live-spec pack withdrew that script after finding no error the script had
615	   ever caught.
616	   A session's opening writes no committed artifact for a script to read. The owner asked for
617	   this reading as a standing process, 2026-07-28.
618	
619	
620	## Work that belongs elsewhere
621	
622	Reserve this file for the pack's own work: a session outside the pack uses a general style guide instead.
623	Never write host- or person-specific values here — those live in profiles, and this file holds only
624	package defaults and the rules themselves. The scope is pack-internal by the owner's decision (recorded
625	2026-07-16). The base serves the pack's skills and the projects that adopted the pack. It is no
626	general-purpose rulebook for unrelated sessions. That decided sentence closes the recurring scope
627	question for good.
628	
629	## The settings ladder
630	
631	How the pack behaves is a **named setting** in one of four nested scopes. Resolution reads from the
632	narrowest scope out — **session beats host beats personal beats package default** (SPEC E-13).
633	
634	The ladder itself is one module in this same package:
635	[references/settings-ladder.md](references/settings-ladder.md), beside this file. It holds the four
636	scopes and their homes. It holds the package-defaults table every setting is a row of. It holds the
637	rule that a budget moves the pace and never the standard.
638	
639	Open that module when a setting is being resolved, proposed, or recorded, and not before. Nothing in
640	it is optional. Nothing in it moved elsewhere: the module is the ladder's one home, read on demand
641	rather than carried by every session that touches no setting.
642	
643	> The pack, whole: **live-spec-base** holds the shared rules and defaults · **spec-author** writes the spec ·
644	> **product-prover** reviews it · **product-prover-pack** binds the external prover to the pack · **design-reviewer** judges the design behind it · **build-pipeline** ships the change · **test-author** derives the matrix and writes the tests · **communicator** makes the human
645	> exchange land · **feedback-intake** brings what comes back to its home · **feedback-collector** offers a rare private note up to the authors · **text-audit** reads a text as a stranger and fixes where they stop · **publish** sees the work out the door, owing its kind's checklist.
